# EAFIT rewards short story writing talent with the National University Microfiction Contest

_**Registration for the 3rd National University Microfiction Contest "Palabras Contadas" (Told Words**_**), led by the Department of Artistic Development of EAFIT, will be open until October 13th.****Students, professors, administrative staff, and graduates from all universities in the country can participate.**

**In its eight years, the competition has received over 470 micro-stories and awarded prizes to winners from across the country, including Cauca, Santander, and the Caribbean coast. All winning stories from previous editions can be found at this link.**

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [News](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias)
- EAFIT Rewards Short Story Writing Talent with the National University Microfiction Contest

![Imagen EAFIT rewards short story writing talent with the National University Microfiction Contest](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/0d21e1e5-343e-4bdd-8942-ac038f0f1240/web/Microrrelato.jpg?crop=yes&k=c&w=823&h=450&itok=8-DyDgrK)

The contest seeks to bring together the university community from all over the country around the written word, reading and literature.

_"Son, draw the letter O." "Look, Mom, they look like truck wheels, the moon when it's pregnant, the number zero, the shadow on my head, my little brother's eyes, Grandpa's rings." "Draw the letter O." "Mom, what if we put them together and make a centipede or a clockwork mechanism? What if each letter O is a bubble that pops and goes 'Splat!', but with an O? What if, Mom, I make you a necklace of letter O's? Did you notice, Mom, that all my hair says OOOOOO?"_

With this story, written in less than 100 words, Angélica María Sierra Franco, professor of undergraduate Architecture at the Corporación Universitaria del Caribe (Cecar), achieved first place in the VII National University Microfiction Contest Palabras Contadas, organized by the Student Development Department of EAFIT in 2022.

Among the 45 participants, the teacher stood out not only for meeting the length requirements, but also for her conciseness, clarity, and creativity. These are precisely the qualities the jury is seeking for the eighth edition of the competition, which will accept applications until October 13th at the following link.

Students, professors, administrative staff, and graduates from all higher education institutions in the country can participate in this contest. The main requirements? Certification that they are part of a higher education institution (in any of the aforementioned categories), and that the micro-stories do not exceed 200 words.

“The beauty of this contest is that it can be a gateway for people who have had some experience with writing, and especially with this genre, to continue refining and enhancing their skills,” says writer Daniel Bravo, one of the judges for this edition.

Daniel points out that, in addition to length, other criteria of form and content that will be taken into account during the evaluation process will focus on the author's style, the coherence of the story, the ability to innovate, or the emotions that the micro-story can produce.

“This is a genre that is gaining a lot of momentum in our country. In fact, in Latin America we have great exponents like Ana María Shua, Eduardo Berti, and Augusto Monterroso, and countries like Argentina, Mexico, and Uruguay stand out for their contributions to microfiction. But we still have a lot to explore, and these kinds of competitions allow us to continue fostering talent,” the jury points out.

###### **A lot to tell in a few words**

Narrating something in just a few words is no easy task. On the surface, it may seem like a short story that only _says_ what is written, but upon closer reading, beneath the carefully chosen verbs, adjectives, and nouns, the reader will discover the true treasure that a microfiction offers.

In higher education institutions, there are creative, sensitive writers capable of conveying these emotions to us. With them and all the stories they have to tell in mind, for the past eight years, the Department of Artistic Development at EAFIT has led the National University Microfiction Contest, "Palabras Contadas" (Told Words), with the aim of encouraging literary thought and creation within university communities throughout the country.

“At the Artistic Development office, we had many proposals to promote creativity and talent in music, dance, theater, and visual arts, and we felt we were missing one: literature. That's how this initiative came to life, one that transcends the boundaries of our campus and brings us all together around the written word and its possibilities,” explains José Daniel Gómez Zapata, head of that EAFIT unit.

For José Daniel, it is also very valuable that this is a space for all people who are part of educational institutions, as he considers that universities are sources of stories, conversations, anecdotes and experiences that can encourage imagination and creativity.

En sus ocho años de trayectoria el galardón ha recibido más de 470 micorrelatos. Entre los ganadores hay personas de diferentes lugares del territorio nacional como Cauca, Santander y la costa Caribe. En esta edición el ganador del primer lugar se llevará un bono digital de 500.000 pesos de la Librería Acentos de EAFIT, y el segundo puesto un bono digital de 300.000 pesos. Así mismo, se realizará la publicación de su cuento en el sitio web de Desarrollo Artístico y en las redes sociales de la Dirección de Desarrollo Humano-Bienestar Universitario.

metadata.ogTitle: EAFIT premia el talento de escribir corto con el Concurso Nacional Universitario de Microrrelato
metadata.ogDescription: -Hijo, dibuja la letra O. -Mira mamá, parecen las ruedas de un camión, la luna cuando está preñada, el cero, la sombra de mi cabeza, los ojos de mi hermanito, las sortijas del abuelo. -Que dibujes la letra O.  -Mamá ¿y si las juntamos y hacemos un ciempiés o el engranaje de un reloj? ¿Y si cada letra O es una burbuja cuando se rompe y hace ¡Plap!, pero con O? ¿Qué tal mamá si te hago un collar de letras O? ¿Te diste cuenta mamá de que todo mi cabello dice O O O O O O?
